alignments.note: Explicit subject of the verbless clause takes only its own English under rule 20.
Predicate adjective takes the construction-supplied copula under rule 20, headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17; *asunder* is the English phrasal particle completing the verb's own lexeme under rule 44, so the head stays on *cut*.
Construct noun with the *the* supplied under rule 29, no article morpheme standing in the phrase.
Anarthrous substantival adjective as nomen rectum: the chain's *of* is its under rule 19 and the supplied *the* completes the substantive under rule 46, headed on *wicked*.

review_notes: Both *the*s are supplied: no article morpheme stands anywhere in the chain, so rule 29 gives one to the construct noun and rule 46 gives the other to the substantival adjective.
